doc: Labelled accuracy set for the content promise / claims check (CT-ACC, 2026-10-22): Content QA §9d (CL.business: terms, scope, credentials) and §9e (CL.commitments: deliverables, process, billing, guarantees, timelines, scope) must flag every statement a written page makes in the business's name that nothing on file supports, and nothing else. One case per sentence. `label`: supported_claim (a statement about the business that the facts on file carry, in any wording), unsupported_claim (a statement about the business that nothing on file supports: the page may not say it until the owner confirms it), not_a_claim (generic statements, advice to the reader, the call to action, quotes from cited sources). `facts` per site: what Content QA reads as the business's own text (OWN_TEXT). `heading` / `h3` / `before` / `list`: where the sentence sits on the page (the check reads a sentence with its section); `section`: for the sentences of the exec 42 page, the whole H2 group they sit in on that page (the scorer reads that section in place of the heading fields). `holdout`: sha1(sentence + site) first byte mod 10 < 3, fixed here so a fixer reports dev and hold-out separately and tunes on dev only. Labels were written from the facts before the code was run and are not changed to pass. Scorer: score_claims.js; scenario CLACC ratchets on CLAIMS_BASELINE.md.

labels.supported_claim: a statement about the business that the facts on file carry (any wording)
labels.unsupported_claim: a statement about the business that nothing on file supports
labels.not_a_claim: not a statement about the business: generic, advice to the reader, call to action, a quote from a source

## How an AI engagement runs, from discovery to governance

[Image: AI engagement phases from discovery to governance]

### Assess & Envision: find the use cases worth funding

This phase covers discovery, requirements, gap-fit analysis against your existing licences and ROI assessment. You receive a prioritised use-case backlog, data readiness findings and an ROI case for each candidate. See our [Assess & Envision discovery and ROI assessment](https://www.techand.ai/whatwedo/assess-envision).

### Build & Implement: from proof of concept to production

We test a proof of concept against your real data and live integrations. We then build for production on Dynamics 365, Microsoft Fabric, Power Platform and Azure AI. You receive a working solution, integration with your systems and documented test results.

### Run & Optimize: monitoring, MLOps and adoption

This phase covers adoption tracking, model monitoring and MLOps, with optional Managed Services and 24/7 support. You receive a runbook and monitoring dashboards. For GCC groups with several entities, Global Rollouts extend a proven solution entity by entity.

### Knowledge transfer: what your team keeps

Handover is a planned workstream, not a final meeting. Admins learn security and licence management. Makers learn to extend Copilot Studio and Power Platform solutions, and business users get role-based training. You keep a self-study pack of documentation, agent playbooks and the runbook. New staff can learn the solution from it, and your team can become its owner.

## Build, buy or integrate: choosing the right AI approach

### Should we build, buy or integrate AI?

Start with the least custom option that meets the requirement. Buy AI already built into tools you license when the process is standard. Integrate and extend with Copilot Studio or AI Builder when you need your own data or workflows. Build on Azure OpenAI Service only when the use case is a differentiator or the data demands it.

**Build, buy or integrate: which AI route fits your use case**

| Route | Typical Microsoft tools | Best when | Integration depth | Data and compliance considerations | Skills your team needs afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy (out of the box) | Copilot for Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 Copilot | The process is standard, such as drafting or summarising | Low: works inside existing apps | Inherits current permissions, so fix oversharing and apply labels first | Admin configuration, user training |
| Integrate and extend | Copilot Studio, AI Builder, Power Platform | You need your own data, workflows or agents without full custom development | Medium: ERP and CRM connectors | Connector governance, data loss prevention policies | Makers and a platform owner |
| Build custom | Azure OpenAI Service, Azure AI Services | The use case is a differentiator or needs retrieval over proprietary documents | High: custom APIs and data pipelines | Region choice, network isolation, logging, model risk review | Developers, machine learning skills, MLOps |

Gap-fit analysis decides the route. If out-of-the-box Copilot covers the requirement, we stop there. Sometimes a rule-based Power Platform workflow solves the problem more cheaply than AI, and we will tell you so.

## AI governance, data residency and UAE compliance

These are questions to put to any consultant, not legal advice. Confirm the obligations that apply to you with your legal and compliance teams.

Which data protection rules apply depends on where your entity is licensed and where personal information is processed.

### Questions to ask about data residency

- Where will personal data and backups be processed and stored?
- Which cloud region will host each component, and does any part run outside the UAE?
- Are prompts and outputs retained or used for training?
- Does federal law, DIFC or ADGM govern our entity?
- What audit evidence will show a regulator how a decision was made?

### Governance controls to have in place before going live

- Access permissions reviewed, because Copilot surfaces whatever a user can already open
- Sensitivity labels applied before switching on Copilot
- Human review for decisions affecting customers or citizens
- AI activity logged and retained in line with policy
- Model monitoring for accuracy and drift

### Can AI pass compliance review in banking and the public sector?

It can, when controls come first. Banks should ask what their regulator expects on model risk and audit trails. Public bodies should ask how government data classification applies. ## AI consultant, data scientist or AI consulting firm: which do you need?

### What is the difference between an AI consultant and a data scientist?

A data scientist analyses data and builds or tunes machine learning models. An AI consultant works a level above. They decide which business problems are worth solving with AI, choose the approach and tools, plan integration with existing systems, and set up governance, training and adoption. Many projects need both roles.

### Independent consultant, consulting firm or in-house team

- **Independent AI consultant:** sharp strategy advice, but limited capacity for integration and continuity.
- **AI consulting firm:** strategy and development under one contract. Check its depth in the ERP and CRM you run.
- **Systems integrator or Microsoft partner:** Dynamics 365, data and security integration, plus support after go-live, such as Tech& Managed Services.
- **In-house team:** long-term ownership, but hiring is slow, and one data scientist cannot cover strategy, integration and governance alone.

Many enterprises combine the two: a firm delivers the first production use cases while internal hires shadow the work and then take over.

Start with the least custom option that meets the requirement. Buy AI already built into tools you license when the process is standard. |---|---|---|---|---|---|

## AI governance, data residency and UAE compliance

These are questions to put to any consultant, not legal advice. Confirm the obligations that apply to you with your legal and compliance teams.

Which data protection rules apply depends on where your entity is licensed and where personal information is processed.

### Questions to ask about data residency

- Where will personal data and backups be processed and stored?
- Which cloud region will host each component, and does any part run outside the UAE?
- Are prompts and outputs retained or used for training?
- Does federal law, DIFC or ADGM govern our entity?
- What audit evidence will show a regulator how a decision was made?

### Governance controls to have in place before going live

- Access permissions reviewed, because Copilot surfaces whatever a user can already open
- Sensitivity labels applied before switching on Copilot
- Human review for decisions affecting customers or citizens
- AI activity logged and retained in line with policy
- Model monitoring for accuracy and drift

### Can AI pass compliance review in banking and the public sector?

It can, when controls come first. Banks should ask what their regulator expects on model risk and audit trails. Public bodies should ask how government data classification applies. We design permissions, labels, logging and human review before any model touches live data, and document each decision for your audit team. a regional bank

We treat data as a sovereign asset. Read more about [our security approach](https://www.techand.ai/security).

### Use cases

- Each candidate use case has a defined process.

### What your score means

- **Readiness assessment:** two or more "no" answers under data or under governance, or any "no" under use cases. AI built on poorly owned data gives answers nobody trusts.

- **Scale-up:** pilots already running, with fewer than two "no" answers under data and under governance. The usual blocker is integration, governance or adoption, not the model.

The role bridges AI technologies and business management. A consultant decides where AI will change a decision or a cost, then gets it there safely.
